# Tooltips and keys {#tooltips}

Hover over any control for a tooltip. This chapter lists every one of them (generated from the program source, so it is always current), the explanations shown on the pattern editor's status line, and the keyboard reference.

## Converter {#tooltips-converter}

| Control | Tooltip |
|---|---|
| Load MOD / XM / SNDH / YM / YMT / WAV… | Open a MOD, XM, SNDH, YM or YMT file, or a WAV / MP3 recording to transcribe (you can also drop a file anywhere on the page) |
| Help | Manual, how-to guide, effects reference and technical specifications (opens in a new tab) |
| Demo: Omar's Bazaar | Load the bundled demo song, Omar's Bazaar by Qumran |
| Converter | Load, convert, listen and export a module |
| AY pattern editor | Edit a song as patterns for one YM2149 (FastTracker 2 style) |
| Subtune | Which subtune of the SNDH file to run |
| Seconds | 0 = use the length from the file's TIME tag |
| STe samples | This tune plays 8-bit samples through the STe DMA sound chip, which a YM2149 register dump cannot carry. On: each sample becomes a 4-bit digidrum hit on voice C at the same frames (voice C is silent while it plays). Off: the samples are left out. |
| Start (s) | Where in the recording the analysis begins |
| Seconds | How much of the recording is analysed (the chip dump is 50 frames per second; long recordings take a few seconds per minute) |
| Voices | How many of the chip's three tone channels the analysis may use. Fewer voices = cleaner results for melodies and bass lines; the noise generator takes a free channel for percussion. |
| Gate (dB) | Notes quieter than this, relative to the loudest passage, are dropped. Lower it to keep soft notes, raise it to get rid of background hiss and reverb tails. |
| Gain (dB) | Extra gain before the 16 volume steps, in dB. Quiet recordings sound thin; loud ones saturate at volume 15. |
| Snap to notes | Pull pitches that are within about a third of a semitone to the nearest note. Off keeps vibrato and slides as they were played (as period changes). |
| Noise | Percussion, breath and cymbals (what is left in the high band after the notes are taken out) become the YM noise generator on a free channel. |
| Edit as AY patterns → | Turn this register dump into an editable pattern song: the tempo and notes are found, every sound becomes a step-table instrument, digidrums and Q/S/U effects come along |
| Level | Overall loudness mapped onto the 16 YM volume steps |
| Drum priority | How strongly kicks/snares/hats win a voice against melody notes |
| Voice stickiness | Higher = a note stays on the same YM voice (less jumping, fewer clicks) |
| Sample waveform → buzzer | Match the sample's waveform: sawtooth, triangle and sine-like tones become the YM's hardware-envelope buzzer (one voice at a time, bass range, loud notes) instead of a square wave. Square and complex samples stay square tones. Each instrument can be set by hand in the table. |
| Bass + drums on the middle voice | How AY composers lay out the three voices: bass and the synthetic drums on the middle voice (B), melody and arpeggios on A and C, so the voices sit in different frequency ranges. Digidrums stay on voice C. |
| Arpeggio | Order in which an arpeggio cycles its notes |
| Arp fill | Notes that would be dropped (more channels than YM voices) share a voice and alternate every 20 ms, like a chiptune chord |
| Min. volume | Dropped notes quieter than this AY volume are not worth an arpeggio slot |
| Percussion as digidrums | Percussion samples (not the tonal ones) are played as real 4-bit samples through a voice's volume register, driven by an MFP timer interrupt. They take voice C while they play. |
| Drum rate | Sample rate of the digidrums; the ST can only make some rates, the nearest one is used. Higher = clearer but costs more CPU and memory. |
| Drum length | Longest digidrum; longer samples are cut (with a short fade) |
| Reset to auto | Back to the automatic settings: options, priorities, instrument roles and names |
| Save mapping | Save the instrument mapping, channel priorities and these options as a .json file |
| Load mapping… | Load a mapping saved earlier (for this module or a similar one) |
| Manual import… | Choose which channels matter most, listen to each channel alone and to the full preview |
| Edit as AY patterns → | Turn the module into an editable pattern song for one YM2149 (uses the options above) |
| SNDH (.sndh) | Playable in any SNDH player (68000 player included, 50 Hz) |
| YM (.ym) | YM5! register dump — ST-Sound, Atari players |
| Game kit (.zip) | C header with the packed stream + ymplay.h replayer |
| Preview (.wav) | 44.1 kHz audio of the YM2149 emulation |
| Raw regs (.regs) | The 14 YM registers of every 50 Hz frame as raw bytes |
| Report (.txt) | The conversion report as a text file |
| ⏮ | Back to the start |
| ■ Stop / ▶ Play | Play or stop the preview (Space) |
| B · YM2149 | The YM2149 version (Tab switches between A and B) |
| Tr. | Transpose in semitones |
| Wave (column of the instrument table) | Waveform of the sample's cycle. A sawtooth / triangle / sine-like tone can be played as the YM's hardware-envelope buzzer (one voice at a time, loud notes in the bass/low range only). |
| AY role (column of the instrument table) | How this instrument is played on the chip: automatic, as written tone, a synthetic kick / snare / hat, a digidrum sample, a custom macro, or muted |
| edit | Edit the per-tick macro of this instrument |
| − | Lower this channel's priority by 1 |
| + | Raise this channel's priority by 1 |
| Preset | Start from a ready-made macro |
| Loop from | Step to jump back to after the last step; −1 = play once, then silent |
| follow note volume (macro editor) | Scale by the note volume of the source module |
| + step | Append a copy of the last step |
| − step | Remove the last step |
| Instrument name field | Rename instrument NN (module name: …). The name is used in the pattern editor and saved with the mapping; empty = module name. |

## Manual import dialog {#tooltips-manual-import-dialog}

| Control | Tooltip |
|---|---|
| ▶ Full preview (YM2149) | Play the whole conversion with the priorities set below; keep changing them while it plays |
| ▶ Original | the original module, for comparison |
| Suggest | busiest pitched channel = Lead, nearly silent channels = Low |
| Solo ▶ (channel table) | Play this channel alone on the chip (click again to stop) |
| Edit as AY patterns → | convert with these priorities into the editable AY pattern view |
| Done | the priorities stay applied to the exports on the Converter tab |
| Instrument name field | Rename instrument NN: the name is used in the pattern editor and saved with the mapping |
| Activity graph | Click to listen to this channel from that point of the song (silent channels: "This channel is silent") |
| Priority levels | Off: leave this channel out of the import · Low: gives way to the others when voices run short · Normal: no preference · High: wins over normal channels · Lead: the melody: keeps its voice almost always |

## Instrument editor {#tooltips-instrument-editor}

| Control | Tooltip |
|---|---|
| Step volume chart | click or drag to draw the volume of each step |
| Preset | Replace the steps with a ready-made macro (keeps the release setting) |
| Loop from step | Step the sound jumps back to after the last one. -1 = play once, then silent. |
| Release | Ticks of fade-out after a key-off (0 = cut at once) |
| Follow note volume | Scale the steps by the note's volume column (3 dB per AY step) |
| Vol | AY volume 0-15 |
| Semitones | Pitch offset in semitones (decimals allowed) |
| Noise | Noise period 1-31, 0 = no noise |
| + | Duplicate this step |
| − | Remove this step |
| close | Close the instrument editor |
| Play C-5 (hold) | Hold to hear the instrument at C-5 |
| Preset | Replaces this instrument with a ready-made sound: chord ornaments, drums, acid bass. Undoable. |
| Sound type | A step table lets you draw the volume, pitch, noise and tone for every 50 Hz tick. The classic type is the YM Tracker's own ADSR / envelope instrument. |
| Noise period (instrument editor) | noise period 0-31 (low = bright) |
| A D S R | Attack, decay and release are in ticks (1 tick = 20 ms at the default tempo); sustain is the AY level 0-15. |
| Volume table | AY levels 0-15, one per tick; the last one is held |
| Arpeggio | Semitone offsets stepped through while the note plays, e.g. 0 4 7 |
| Arp speed | Ticks per arpeggio step |
| Pitch table | Period offsets added per tick (positive = lower pitch) |
| Vibrato | Speed and depth applied to every note of this instrument (0 depth = off) |
| Sync-square | Restarts the square wave at the start of every note (a very short period is written for 8 PSG clocks, then the real one), so every note starts in the same phase: tight, punchy bass attacks and thin pulses. Needs the SNDH or game-kit player (not YM files) and an STFM-style 4:1 CPU/PSG clock; the STE can miss the edge. |
| Hard envelope | The YM2149's own envelope generator: buzzy bass and synth sounds. One envelope is shared by all three voices. |
| Env. period divisor (÷) | envelope period = tone period ÷ this |

## Status line explanations (effects) {#tooltips-status}

The line under the pattern shows these when the cursor is on a cell with an effect:

| Effect | Explanation |
|---|---|
| `0` | Arpeggio: x and y are semitones added in turn (0xy) |
| `1` | Slide up (1xx) per tick |
| `2` | Slide down (2xx) per tick |
| `3` | Slide to the note (3xx) |
| `4` | Vibrato: x speed, y depth (4xy) |
| `5` | Slide to note + volume slide |
| `6` | Vibrato + volume slide |
| `7` | Tremolo: x speed, y depth |
| `8` | Not played (panning in FastTracker 2) |
| `9` | Not played (sample offset in FastTracker 2) |
| `A` | Volume slide: x up, y down |
| `B` | Jump to song position (Bxx) |
| `C` | Set volume 00-40 |
| `D` | Pattern break to row (Dxx, decimal digits) |
| `E` | Extended: E1y fine up, E2y fine down, ECy cut after y ticks, EDy delay y ticks, EAy/EBy fine volume |
| `F` | Speed (F01-F1F ticks per row) or tempo (F20-FFF BPM) |
| `G` | Global volume 00-40 |
| `H` | Global volume slide |
| `K` | Key off (release the note) |
| `L` | Set envelope position |
| `M` | Envelope period, low byte (Mxx; period = Y*256 + M, overrides the instrument) |
| `P` | Envelope divisor (Pxx): envelope period = tone period / xx |
| `R` | Retrigger every y ticks with volume change x (Rxy); R00 restarts the envelope shape |
| `T` | Reserved (YM Tracker compatibility), not played |
| `X` | Force hardware envelope with shape y (Xxy) |
| `Y` | Envelope period, high byte (Yxx; period = Y*256 + M, overrides the instrument) |
| `Q` | SID voice: the voice volume toggles on/off at a timer rate, 20 Hz * 2^(octave y + pitch x/16). Q00 or a new note ends it |
| `S` | Sinus-SID: like Q, but the "on" half is a sine wave. S00 or a new note ends it |
| `U` | Sync-buzzer: the hardware envelope restarts at a timer rate (use an envelope instrument). U00 or a new note ends it |
| `Z` | Trigger digidrum (Z00 stops) |

## Keyboard reference {#tooltips-keys}

| Keys | Action |
|---|---|
| Z S X D C V G B H N J M , L . | notes of the lower octave; Q 2 W 3 E R 5 T 6 Y 7 U I 9 O the octave above. F1–F8 set the octave. |
| Space | stop playback, or switch Edit on/off · `Right Ctrl` play song · `Right Alt` play pattern · `Right Shift` record pattern |
| Caps Lock / 1 | note off (===) · ``` or `§` cycles the "Add" step (Shift = backwards) |
| Arrows, Tab | move cursor (Tab / Shift+Tab = next / previous channel), Home / End / PgUp / PgDn |
| Shift+←/→ · Ctrl+←/→ | previous / next song position · previous / next pattern number at this position |
| Alt+arrows | select a block (Shift+↑/↓ too); mouse drag and Shift+click also work |
| Del | clear what the cursor column holds · Shift = whole cell · Ctrl = volume + effect · Alt = effect |
| Insert / Backspace | insert / delete a cell in this channel (Shift = whole row) |
| Shift / Ctrl+Shift / Alt + F3 F4 F5 | cut / copy / paste the track / the pattern / the block |
| Ctrl / Alt / Shift + V | scale volume in block / track / pattern (Ctrl+Shift = whole song) |
| Ctrl+Z · Ctrl+Y · Ctrl+S | undo · redo · save .ymt |
| Effect column | type 0–9 A–H K L M P R T X Y Q S U Z (Q SID voice, S sinus-SID, U sync-buzzer: see the hint line). Digits typed in the parameter without an effect make an arpeggio (047 = major chord). |
